If I dual boot, then decide to remove Windows, can I implement full disk encryption afterwards? I see it's an option during solo installs.

Yes, but it's convoluted. It involves deleting the Windows partition, making a new encrypted partition in its place, moving your root drive over to this new partition, deleting the old one, resizing the new one, then editing the boot loader to deal with an encrypted root drive, and you'll be doing all of this largely from the cli of a boot disk.

There may be better alternatives... That's just me spitballing in bed.

This is pretty much it. Dual booting doesn't prevent you from use FDE (since you normally only encrypt a single partition, not the entire drive), but converting an existing, unencrypted install to FDE is annoying because you have to copy the files somewhere else while you reformat the partition.

(Note that resizing an existing partition is considered to be risky by some - I'd definitely back up the contents to a separate partition/drive first, just in case.)
